I might rehearse my lines over and over, but when the moment comes, my voice might sound shaky, and I might mumble or stumble over my words. I might try to avoid eye contact with the audience, hoping they won't notice my nervousness. I might also have a tendency to undervalue my own thoughts and ideas, making me feel like what I have to say isn<nobr> </nobr>important or interesting enough for others to listen to.

Despite these feelings, I try to remind myself that everyone gets nervous, and it's okay to not be perfect. I take deep breaths to calm my nerves and try to focus on the message I want to convey rather than my own anxiety. With practice and time, speaking in public can become less intimidating, and I can learn to embrace my voice and share my thoughts with others.
